defects.summary: A hollow assertion the branch already screened twice and cleared: `assert_not_contains "$msg" "so the pin does not move and"` cannot catch the regression it exists for, because the needle spans the current claim text's own line wrap.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5364, against claim_text_commit_body_format at scripts/lib/bump-pr-claims.sh:311-317, which reads "…so the primary's pin does not\nmove and every digest of its own bundles is recomputed…". The false claim being forbidden is a format+federated commit body saying no pin moved. I made it reappear with a ONE-WORD edit — `sed -i "s/so the primary's pin does not/so the pin does not/"` — which yields "so the pin does not\nmove and", i.e. exactly the sentence the assertion is named after, and test_bump_format_and_federated came back 19 passed / 0 failed, EXIT=0. Only the two-part edit (drop the qualifier AND unwrap the line) reds it: joining the two lines gives 18 passed / 1 failed. This is the very trap the branch documents twice in its own comments — "EACH NEEDLE STOPS AT THE LINE BREAK THE ORIGINAL COMMENT HAD… a needle spelling out a sentence that was wrapped across two comment lines matches nothing in EITHER version — a green light wired to nothing" (test/run-tests.sh:7568-7572) — applied to comment needles and missed on this artifact needle. The round-3 fix report screened it and concluded "Proven wired anyway: un-qualifying the claim in claim_text_commit_body_format back to a single line reds it"; un-qualifying it WITHOUT also unwrapping is the realistic edit and it does not.

defects.summary: Round 2's self_named defect is only half closed. The PR body was split into scoped/degraded claims, but the log() line round 2 named in the same defect still gives the degraded run the reason it cannot stand behind — so the two artifacts of one run now contradict each other.
defects.evidence: scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1142, unchanged since c7e5569 (grep -c of the full sentence: 1 then, 1 now) and unguarded by $FED_ADVANCE_AVAILABLE. Round 2's defect text named it explicitly: "(and the matching log() at :1125) … Same log line fires in degraded mode with the same wrong reason." Round 3's resolutions list marks that defect "fixed" with evidence covering only the two body claims. Measured end to end: I stood up a self-federating lock (bumporg/agentskills as both primary and a source) and ran the bumper with a stub whose scoped flags were stripped by the suite's own strip-scoped-flags.py. The run emits `::warning::… has no '--check-current --only <REGISTRY>'` and then logs `skills.lock names bumporg/agentskills as both its primary registry and a federated source; a scoped question under that one name has two answers, so it is not put and that entry's pin is carried through untouched.` — while the PR body of the SAME run correctly says "No per-source question was put about any source in this run, and this generator has no flag that could scope one to a name meaning two things in any case." The log states a refusal by a generator that has no such flag; the body says the opposite. Nothing in the claims library governs log() output, and no test covers a degraded self-federating lock.

defects.summary: The replacement for "the whole of it" still under-names what the run appended: the invocation also adds `--source-repo`, without which the reconstructed command cannot run at all.
defects.evidence: claim_text_repro_shape_half (scripts/lib/bump-pr-claims.sh:419-424) renders "**That remediation line is the SHAPE half of the command this PR ran**, `--ref` included. This run appended `--repin-source 'org/src@'` to it…". The quoted remediation line is the generator's own (test/run-tests.sh:1024-1026): `python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref <sha> --repo <a clone of the registry this lock names> -o <this lock>` — no `--source-repo`. The actual invocation at scripts/bump-consumer-locks.sh:1492-1498 passes `--repo`, the `--ref` args, the `--repin-source` args, `${source_repo_args[@]}` AND `-o`. Round 2 established (V0.D0/#65 work) that a federated re-pin without `--source-repo` exits with `ERROR: <reg>: no checkout — pass --source-repo`. So a reader who takes the quoted line and appends the flags the body names gets a command that fails. The claim is incomplete rather than false — strictly better than "the whole of it" — but `repin_source_flags_shown` is built only from fed_drifted_regs and structurally cannot mention the other addition. No cross-product prohibition covers under-naming an addition; r_whole only forbids the string 'whole of it'.

defects.summary: A universal quantifier the run did not establish, in the file written to make that impossible: on a lock with a self-named `sources` entry, the federated header says every source was asked — and two paragraphs later the body says one was not.
defects.evidence: claim_text_federated_advanced (scripts/lib/bump-pr-claims.sh:603-609) — "Each source was put its OWN `--check-current --only <registry>` question" — and claim_text_federated_unchanged (:610-616) — "Each was put its own `--check-current --only <registry>` question and answered that its bundles have not moved". Both arms check only CLAIM_LISTED_SOURCES/CLAIM_SCOPED_AVAILABLE/CLAIM_FED_ADVANCED; neither reads CLAIM_SELF_NAMED. Rendered by me for reason=content, sources=(org/reg org/src), scoped=true, nothing drifted: the body prints "Each was put its own … question and answered that its bundles have not moved" over a one-bullet list, then "**One `sources` entry names `org/reg`… A `--check-current --only org/reg` has two answers under that one name, so the question was not put**". Same shape for the advanced variant (federated--self_named_plus--true). This is structurally the round-2 'and nothing else' / 'moved too' defect — a header quantifier denied further down the same body — differing only in that this one is reconciled rather than left contradicting. The cross-product's nine prohibitions contain nothing that could catch it; it is the seventh shape the fix report's stillOpen note predicted.

defects.summary: One of the two directions of the new stub-inventory assertion is vacuous: any stand-in whose name shares an interpolated prefix can be listed and never built, and the check stays green.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5535-5541. The checker collects `interp = {u.split("$")[0] for u in used if "$" in u}` — today exactly {'generator-missing-'} from `gen="$TEST_DIR/generator-missing-$which.py"` at :6242 — and then skips the listed-but-never-built complaint for any listed name that `startswith` such a prefix. So `generator-missing-only.py` and `generator-missing-repin-source.py` vouch for each other. Proven: `sed -i '6241s/for which in only repin-source; do/for which in only; do/'` leaves generator-missing-repin-source.py listed in the inventory and built by nothing, and test_bump_stub_generator_parity returns `PASS: stub inventory: it names every stand-in in this file, and only those, in the numbers it states`, 12 passed / 0 failed, EXIT=0. The other direction (built but not listed) and both number-word checks do fail correctly, so the assertion is not hollow — but the label claims a completeness it does not have.

defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5492-5495: "The four hand-rolled ones carry neither `--only` nor `--repin-source`, so both federated probes degrade in their lanes and emit a `::warning::` apiece." One of those four is generator-no-repin.py, whose own bullet at :5468-5469 says "the run exits 2 at the one HARD probe before any flag here matters". I ran test_bump_generator_without_repin in isolation and dumped its captured log — one ERROR line, `::warning::` count = 0. Secondary: the block heads a FIVE-bullet list "HAND-ROLLED" and then says "The four hand-rolled ones"; the checker encodes the off-by-one as `len(hand) - 1` rather than the comment saying "the four besides write_stub_generator", so a reader counting the list against the sentence finds the same five-versus-four mismatch round 2 filed. 787b0dc rewrote this sentence (from "The last four") as part of the count fix and left the consequence clause wrong.

defects.summary: Dead code in the new inventory checker: `stated` is assigned by one regex and immediately overwritten by another on the next line.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5518-5519 — `stated = re.search(r"^# (\w+)\n?# ?generator stand-ins|^# ([A-Z]+)\b generator stand-ins", block, re.M)` followed directly by `stated = re.search(r"([A-Z]+) *\n?#? *generator stand-ins", block)`. The first result is never read. Only the second regex is load-bearing, so the first is an abandoned attempt shipped in the same commit that added the assertion. Harmless at runtime, but it is unreviewed leftovers in a brand-new gate and reads as if two patterns are being tried.

defects.summary: The slice test's comment claims it "runs the exact pipeline", but it re-types the pipeline and verifies only half of it against the library.
defects.evidence: test/run-tests.sh:5779-5781 ("this test is what makes the claim checkable — it runs the exact pipeline over a synthetic stream") and :5808 (`sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' "$stream" | head -20 > "$sliced"`). The derivation guard at :5788 greps the library for the literal `fed_check_out" | head -20` only, so the `head -20` half cannot drift silently — but the `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p'` range is a hand copy. Change the library's range (say to `/^FAILED:/,+5p`) and this test keeps measuring the old pipeline while its comment says it runs the current one. Proven that the guarded half is live: `sed -i 's/fed_check_out" | head -20/…head -19/g'` on the lib reds `slice: the claims library really caps the federated slice at 20 lines` and short-circuits the test.
